verses.text: This is where the good news about Jesus Christ, God’s Son, begins.
As the prophets wrote: “Look, I’m sending my messenger ahead of you; he’ll prepare your way.
He’s a voice calling out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the Lord’s way! Make his paths straight!’”
John appeared in the wilderness, baptizing and preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
People from the whole Judean countryside and Jerusalem came out to him. As they confessed their sins, John baptized them in the Jordan River.
John wore clothes made of camel hair with a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
He preached, “Someone stronger than me is coming after me. I’m not even worthy to bend down and untie his sandal straps.
I baptized you with water, but he’ll baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
Around that time, Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee, and John baptized him in the Jordan.
As Jesus came up out of the water, he saw the heavens split open and the Spirit coming down on him like a dove.
A voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son. I’m pleased with you.”
Right away, the Spirit sent him out into the wilderness.
He was there for forty days, tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and angels took care of him.
After John was arrested, Jesus went into Galilee, announcing God’s good news.
He said, “The time has come! God’s kingdom is near. Turn back and believe the good news.”
As Jesus walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew throwing a net into the water. They were fishermen.
Jesus said, “Come follow me, and I’ll teach you to fish for people.”
They immediately left their nets and followed him.
A little farther along, he saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat mending their nets.
He called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and followed him.
They went to Capernaum. On the Sabbath, Jesus went into the synagogue and began teaching.
People were amazed at his teaching, because he taught with authority, unlike the legal experts.
Just then, a man with an impure spirit was in their synagogue, and he shouted,
“What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!”
Jesus ordered him, “Be quiet! Come out of him!”
The impure spirit shook the man violently, cried out, and came out of him.
Everyone was stunned and asked each other, “What’s this? A new teaching—and with authority! He even commands impure spirits, and they obey him!”
News about Jesus quickly spread throughout the whole region of Galilee.
As soon as they left the synagogue, they went with James and John to the home of Simon and Andrew.
Simon’s mother-in-law was in bed with a fever, and they told Jesus about her right away.
He went to her, took her hand, and helped her up. The fever left her, and she began serving them.
That evening after sunset, people brought Jesus everyone who was sick or possessed by demons.
The whole town gathered at the door.
Jesus healed many people with all kinds of diseases and drove out many demons. He wouldn’t let the demons speak, because they knew who he was.
Very early the next morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up, went outside, and headed to a quiet place to pray.
Simon and the others went searching for him.
When they found him, they said, “Everyone’s looking for you.”
He replied, “Let’s go to the nearby towns so I can preach there too. That’s why I came.”
He traveled throughout Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and driving out demons.
A man with a skin disease came to Jesus. He begged him, knelt down, and said, “If you’re willing, you can make me clean.”
Jesus was moved with compassion. He reached out, touched him, and said, “I am willing. Be clean!”
Immediately the disease left him, and he was clean.
Jesus sent him away at once, sternly warning him,
“Don’t tell anyone. Go show yourself to the priest, and bring the offering Moses commanded for your cleansing as a testimony to them.”

But the man went out and started telling everyone what happened, spreading the news everywhere. As a result, Jesus could no longer enter a town openly. He stayed outside in quiet places, but people came to him from all over.
